name: Plug-in Edit Page
apex: The definition screen for a plug-in (item, region, dynamic action, process, authorization, authentication, or REST source type) where a developer sets its name, source callbacks, custom attributes, files, attribute groups and events.
workflow: Shared Components > Plug-ins > select a plug-in > edit any section > Apply Changes.
relevance: This is the shape a Paddock component-type definition screen needs: one record per component type with settings/attributes/files/events sub-sections, exactly what Component Settings should evolve toward.

name: Custom Attributes / Attribute Scope
apex: Plug-in-defined settings a developer fills in per use; each attribute declares a Scope of Application (once per app), Component (per instance), Report or Report Group (multi-row regions only).
workflow: Developer adds an attribute, picks its scope and type, and it appears as a property-panel field wherever the plug-in is used.
relevance: Paddock's Component Settings should let an attribute be scoped app-wide vs per-region-instance the same way, instead of only supporting one flat settings bag.

name: Plug-in Attribute Types
apex: The fixed set of editor types APEX offers for a custom plug-in attribute, each rendering a matching control and validator in Page Designer's property panel.
workflow: Developer picks a Type per attribute so the right widget (color picker, icon picker, code editor, link builder) and validation appear automatically.
relevance: Direct template for Paddock's Component Settings attribute editors: color/icon pickers, code editors, link builders and a boolean toggle are exactly the control set a general-component settings tab needs.

name: Plug-in Files / File Prefix
apex: Lets a plug-in bundle its own CSS/JS/image files, stored in the database or on a web server, addressed by a configurable File Prefix (or #APEX_FILES#).
workflow: Developer uploads a file under a directory path, then references it from plug-in code via the file prefix substitution.
relevance: Next.js already bundles and serves each component's assets at build time; there is no need for a component to declare its own runtime file prefix or database-stored asset store.
skip_for_web: Solves a problem the Next.js build pipeline already solves.

name: File URLs to Load (auto CSS/JS injection)
apex: Attributes listing CSS and JavaScript URLs that APEX automatically emits into the page template whenever the plug-in is used, with #MIN#/#MIN_DIRECTORY#/#PLUGIN_FILES# substitutions for minified vs debug builds.
workflow: Developer lists file URLs, one per line; APEX injects them once per page that uses the plug-in, swapping in minified paths outside debug mode.
relevance: Webpack/Turbopack already dedupes and minifies per-component JS/CSS at build time; Paddock components import their own assets rather than declaring URLs for a runtime injector.
skip_for_web: Manual per-page asset injection is what a modern bundler replaces.

name: Attribute Groups
apex: Named, sequenced sections (Item/Region/Process/Dynamic Action plug-ins only) that cluster related custom attributes together in Page Designer's property panel; ungrouped attributes fall under a generic Settings heading.
workflow: Developer adds a group with a title and sequence, then assigns each custom attribute to it via the attribute's Group field.
relevance: Paddock's Component Settings tab should group related attributes into named, ordered sections instead of one flat list, exactly this pattern.

name: Plug-in Events
apex: Named JavaScript events an item/region/dynamic-action plug-in can expose (a display Name plus the underlying Internal Name, e.g. a jQuery event) so page authors can attach Dynamic Actions to them.
workflow: Plug-in developer registers an event name and its JS event; page developers then pick that event as a Dynamic Action trigger, same as a built-in Change or Click event.
relevance: If Paddock's designer ever lets one component react to another's interaction (e.g. a filter component signalling a list region), components need to declare named events other logic can subscribe to, same idea.

name: Copying or Subscribing to a Plug-in
apex: Wizard to copy a plug-in definition from another application in the workspace (optionally scoped to one theme's Template Component plug-ins), with an option to copy-and-subscribe so it stays linked to the source.
workflow: Developer picks a source app (and optional theme), names the copy, and chooses whether to also subscribe to the master.
relevance: Paddock is one application, not many workspace apps sharing plug-ins; there is no cross-app copy step for a single-tenant site.
skip_for_web: Multi-application component reuse doesn't apply to a single Next.js codebase.

name: Deleting a Plug-in
apex: Plug-ins can only be deleted when unused; the Delete button is hidden on the Edit page if the plug-in is referenced anywhere in the app.
workflow: Developer opens the plug-in's Edit page; Delete only appears once every usage has been removed.
relevance: Paddock's shared component registry (Lists, Component Settings) should hide/block Delete the same way whenever a component definition is still referenced by a page.

name: Plug-in Repository
apex: A central Oracle Technology Network catalog where developers publish and download community plug-ins, reachable from the Plug-ins page.
workflow: Developer clicks a link to browse and download third-party plug-ins from OTN.
relevance: Paddock has no external component marketplace and building one is out of scope for a content site's own designer.
skip_for_web: External Oracle-hosted marketplace, not a pattern to replicate.

name: Resetting the Plug-in Interactive Report
apex: A Reset button that clears any filters/sorts a developer has applied to the Plug-ins list report itself.
workflow: Click Reset on the Plug-ins page to clear the report's current filters.
relevance: Generic interactive-report chrome already covered by earlier Interactive Report notes; nothing plug-in specific to learn.
skip_for_web: Standard IR reset control.

name: Plug-in Utilization Page
apex: A report showing every page, component and region across the application that currently uses a given plug-in.
workflow: Developer clicks Utilization from the Plug-ins page to see where a plug-in is actually used before changing or removing it.
relevance: Paddock Developer's component registry should offer the same reverse lookup, an impact report of every page/region using a shared component before it's edited or deleted.

name: Plug-in History Page
apex: An audit log of actions taken on a plug-in (what changed, which developer, when).
workflow: Developer clicks History from the Plug-ins page to see the change trail for that shared component.
relevance: Same audit-trail idea Paddock should apply to shared components (Lists, Component Settings) so changes to widely-used definitions are traceable to a person and date.

name: jQuery / jQuery Migrate Support
apex: APEX bundles a specific jQuery version and offers an Include jQuery Migrate toggle so older applications relying on removed 1.x/2.x jQuery APIs keep working.
workflow: Developer enables the Migrate plug-in only if legacy app JavaScript depends on removed jQuery APIs.
relevance: Paddock is React/Next.js, not jQuery-based; there is no equivalent library-version migration switch to learn from.
skip_for_web: jQuery-version compatibility is irrelevant to a React codebase.

name: Manually Refreshing APEX Components
apex: A JavaScript API, apex.region('id').refresh(), that lets custom code trigger a re-fetch/re-render of any region that supports refresh, outside of the Dynamic Action framework.
workflow: Developer calls this one-liner from custom JS when a region needs to reload without a full page action.
relevance: React's own state/re-render model already covers this; there's no matching imperative jQuery-plugin-region API to imitate.
skip_for_web: Solves a jQuery-plugin-region refresh problem that doesn't exist in a React component tree.

name: Automations Disabled After Import
apex: Oracle APEX auto-disables every Automation after an application import so re-importing the same app repeatedly can't spin up duplicate concurrently-running schedules; APEX_AUTOMATION.enable/reschedule re-arms one from PL/SQL.
workflow: After import, a developer explicitly re-enables or reschedules each automation via a PL/SQL call rather than it resuming automatically.
relevance: Any future Paddock feature that duplicates/clones a page or component carrying a scheduled or triggered action should default it to off, to avoid double-execution.

name: Automation (shared component)
apex: A Shared Component that runs a query on a schedule (or on demand) and executes one or more per-row PL/SQL actions, each with its own server-side condition, similar to a lightweight background-job/cron feature built into the app.
workflow: Developer wizards through name+schedule, then source query, then edits each Action's PL/SQL and condition, then Save and Run to test before enabling the schedule.
relevance: The shape (schedule/trigger, a query producing rows, one action per row, a condition, Save-and-Run-to-test) is a reasonable template if Paddock adds background jobs for approvals, e.g. auto-expiring stale author requests or nightly moderation digests.

name: Automation Attributes (full set)
apex: The complete configuration surface for an Automation: schedule status and calendaring expression, error handling per action, and optional init/before-row/cleanup PL/SQL hooks around the row loop.
workflow: Developer sets error-handling policy and optional init/cleanup hooks once, separate from the per-row action logic.
relevance: If Paddock builds a background-job engine for approvals, this is a good checklist: an explicit error policy, a max-rows safety valve, and init/cleanup hooks separate from per-item logic.

name: Automation Execution Log
apex: A per-run log (start/end timestamps, success/error row counts, drill-down Messages) for every Automation execution, purgeable on demand and auto-purged after a configurable retention period.
workflow: Developer reviews the log after Save and Run, drills into Messages for per-row detail, and purges old runs from the same page.
relevance: Any Paddock background job (approval auto-actions, digests) needs the same visible run history with per-item messages and a manual/auto purge, not just a fire-and-forget script.

name: Automation History Report
apex: An audit report of edits made to an Automation's definition itself (as opposed to its execution log), showing Audit Date, Action, Developer and Object Type.
workflow: Developer opens the History tab on the Automations page to see who last changed a given automation and how.
relevance: Same definition-audit-trail pattern already captured for Plug-in History; no new concept beyond repeating it for a different shared-component type.
skip_for_web: Duplicate of the generic component History-tab pattern.

name: Workflows (overview)
apex: A built-in business-process engine: developers model a sequence of activities that move a request between participants through defined states, monitored via a console, and started from a page process.
workflow: Developer authors a workflow definition in the Designer, activates a version, and triggers it from a page process; participants and admins track it in the Console.
relevance: This is the closest APEX concept to Paddock's approval flows (author requests, moderation, post review): a named process with states, participants and a monitoring console is exactly the shape those flows need.

name: Workflow Versions
apex: Each workflow definition has versions in one of three states: In Development (editable, developer-session only), Active (the one live version, partially editable), or Inactive (retired, deletable, cannot start new instances).
workflow: Developer edits the In Development version, then activates it, which automatically demotes the prior Active version to Inactive; running instances keep running on their original version.
relevance: Paddock should let an admin edit a draft version of an approval flow's rules without disturbing in-flight approvals, then promote it, the same draft/active/retired split.

name: Workflow Definitions (Parameters/Variables/Activities/Connections/Participants)
apex: The five building blocks of a workflow definition: Parameters (inputs at start), Variables (mutable during the run), Activities (steps), Connections (paths between steps) and Participants (who can operate it), all managed as a Shared Component.
workflow: Developer builds a workflow by adding each of these five pieces under a workflow version in the Designer tree.
relevance: A clean five-part model (inputs, mutable state, steps, transitions, who's allowed to act) is a good target shape for Paddock's own approval/moderation definitions instead of ad hoc status columns.

name: Workflow Parameters vs Variables
apex: Parameters are fixed inputs passed in once when a workflow instance starts (direction In/Out/In-Out, typed); Variables are mutable values scoped to a workflow version that activities update as the run progresses.
workflow: Developer defines the inputs a workflow needs as Parameters, and any values that change during the run (e.g. an approval decision) as Variables.
relevance: Paddock's approval flows need this same split: fixed context passed in (which post, which author) versus evolving state (current reviewer, decision, comments) updated as the request moves along.

name: Workflow Activities
apex: A logical step in a workflow, each backed by a process-type plugin (Execute Code, Send E-Mail, Human Task - Create, Send Push Notification, Invoke API, Server Side Geocoding, plus workflow-only types Workflow Start/End, Wait, Workflow Switch, Invoke Workflow); every workflow has exactly one Start and at least one End.
workflow: Developer drags an activity type onto the diagram, configures its properties, and wires error handling via Error Connections rather than on the activity itself.
relevance: The activity type list (a human approval step, a notification step, an API call step, a branching switch, a wait/delay) is a strong checklist for the step types a Paddock approval/moderation flow actually needs.

name: Parallel Flow (activities)
apex: A workflow activity type containing two or more branches that execute simultaneously, each branch getting its own activities, with an optional overall deadline that terminates every branch when reached.
workflow: Developer models simultaneous independent steps (e.g. multiple departments onboarding a new hire) as branches inside one parallel flow activity instead of a strict sequence.
relevance: Useful if Paddock ever needs concurrent independent approvals (e.g. both an editor AND a category owner must sign off on a post) rather than assuming every approval is a single linear chain.

name: Workflow Connections (Branches and Transitions)
apex: Links between activities: Branches come from switch activities splitting on a condition result; Transitions go directly activity-to-activity and are typed Normal (default path), Timeout (fires if the Due On deadline passes) or Error (fires on a specific SQL error code instead of faulting the workflow).
workflow: Developer draws a connection between two activities and picks its type; error connections let a workflow recover from a failure instead of going faulted.
relevance: An explicit Timeout and Error transition type, distinct from the normal happy path, is exactly what a robust approval flow needs (e.g. auto-escalate an unreviewed post after N days, or route a failed action to a fallback step).

name: Workflow Participants
apex: APEX users with operational rights over a specific workflow version: a Workflow Owner can start/terminate/retry an instance; a Workflow Administrator can also suspend, resume and edit variable values; the Initiator (whoever started it) can terminate only their own instances.
workflow: Developer assigns Owners/Administrators on the workflow version; any active workflow must have participants specified before it can start.
relevance: Directly maps onto Paddock's Members/Moderation roles: an owner-like role that can act on a request, an admin-like role with full control (suspend/resume/edit), and the requester who can only cancel their own submission.

name: Workflow Designer
apex: A visual, drag-and-drop diagram editor (tree pane, activities palette, diagram builder, toolbar) for authoring a workflow's activities and connections, with error markers surfaced directly on the diagram.
attributes: Diagram Toolbar (zoom, router style, navigator view)
workflow: Developer drags activity types from the palette onto the canvas, connects them, and fixes any activity flagged with a red error icon before saving.
relevance: Building a full drag-and-drop flowchart editor is a large investment Paddock's content-site scale doesn't justify; a simpler linear step-list config UI can cover the same approval logic without a diagram canvas.
skip_for_web: A graphical BPMN-style diagram builder is disproportionate for a handful of content approval flows.

name: Workflow Console, Details and Dashboard
apex: Three generated pages: a Console list (report contexts My Workflows / Admin Workflows / Initiated by Me), a Details page per instance (activity states, variables, parameters, audit history, read-only diagram, suspend/resume/terminate/retry actions), and a Dashboard with state/performance charts.
attributes: Report Context: My Workflows/Admin Workflows/Initiated by Me
Workflow Details: activity states, variables, parameters, audit history
Dashboard: Workflows by State, Active, Faulted, Performance
workflow: Developer generates all three pages via a wizard, then a participant reviews and acts on their workflows in the Console/Details, while admins watch aggregate health in the Dashboard.
relevance: This is close to the exact shape Paddock's Members and Moderation screens should take: a My Requests / All Requests / Requested by Me list, a details view with full history and action buttons, and a health dashboard of pending/stuck items.

name: Workflow Runtime Engine
apex: The engine that executes workflow instances: new instances run the Active version (or the In Development version inside a developer session); execution order follows the connections, not the tree's display sequence; parallel branches interleave nondeterministically.
attributes: Active vs In Development instance selection
workflow: Developer relies on connections (not tree ordering) to control execution order, and tests both the in-development and incognito/active paths before promoting a version.
relevance: The dev-session-sees-draft-version, everyone-else-sees-active-version split is a genuinely useful safe-preview pattern for testing a changed approval flow without affecting live requests.

name: Workflow States and Transitions
apex: A workflow instance is always in exactly one of five states: Active, Suspended, Completed, Terminated or Faulted, with a defined table of which states can move to which others and why (e.g. Faulted can be retried back to Active).
workflow: Workflow Administrators retry a Faulted instance after fixing variables, or suspend/resume/terminate via API or the Details page.
relevance: This is exactly the state machine Paddock should give an approval/moderation request instead of a free-text status column: a fixed small set of states with an explicit, documented transition table.

name: Activity States and Transitions
apex: Each individual activity instance within a workflow also has its own state (Active, Waiting, Completed, Terminated, Faulted), nested under the parent workflow's state, e.g. an activity in Waiting while it holds for a human approval.
workflow: Developer relies on the Waiting state to represent an activity pending a human task or async call, distinct from the workflow's own overall state.
relevance: A per-step state nested inside the overall request state (e.g. this particular reviewer's step is Waiting while the request overall is Active) is a useful two-level model for a multi-step Paddock approval.

name: Example: Sample Workflows, Approvals, and Tasks app
apex: A gallery sample app demonstrating combined workflow/task usage: employee record changes (Salary, Job, Bank) use approval tasks, an Appraisal uses a multi-participant workflow, and a Laptop request combines an approval task, an action task, and a workflow completed programmatically on delivery.
workflow: Developer installs the sample from the App Gallery to see how approval tasks, action tasks and workflows combine for a realistic request-and-approve scenario.
relevance: A worked reference for structuring Paddock's own scenarios: e.g. an author request as a single approval task, but a multi-step post review (edit, fact-check, publish) as a small workflow with participants per step.

name: Creating a Workflow (procedure)
apex: High-level build order for a workflow: create it under Shared Components, name/title it, add Parameters/Activities/Variables/Participants/Connections via right-click context menus, save the definition, wire it into a page process, then activate the version.
workflow: Developer works through the pieces in order (parameters, then activities and connections, then variables and participants), saves, attaches to a page process, and only then activates the version.
relevance: A sensible authoring order (define inputs, then steps and paths, then who can act, save as draft, attach to a trigger, activate last) is a reasonable checklist for a Paddock approval-flow builder.

name: Workflow Parameter Attributes
apex: Fields a developer sets per parameter: a Static ID, display Label, one of a fixed set of data types, a Direction, whether it's Required, a Default Value, and optional format masks.
workflow: Developer fills in this attribute set once per parameter when defining what a workflow instance needs at start.
relevance: Reasonable field list but it's a restatement of the Parameters concept already captured; no new idea beyond the earlier Workflow Parameters vs Variables note.
skip_for_web: Attribute-level detail of a concept already logged.

name: Creating a Workflow Variable (detail)
apex: Variables can only be added while the workflow version is In Development, never on an Active version; a variable's initial Value can come from a Static Value, an Item, a SQL Query, an Expression, a Function Body, or Null.
attributes: Value source: Static Value/Item/SQL Query/Expression/Function Body/Null
workflow: Developer sets a variable's initial value from any of several computed sources, not just a literal.
relevance: Restates the Parameters vs Variables concept already logged; the only new detail (structural edits locked once Active) is covered by the Workflow Versions note.
skip_for_web: Attribute-level duplicate of an already-captured concept.

name: Connection/Participant Validation (Show Messages)
apex: Both the connection and participant editors expose a Show Messages icon listing every workflow modeling/configuration error; clicking an error focuses the offending activity, and APEX blocks Save until all errors are resolved.
workflow: Developer keeps building the diagram, checks Show Messages before saving, and fixes each flagged issue in place.
relevance: A nested visual builder (an approval-flow or page layout editor) should surface a single running list of validation errors that jump to the offending element, rather than only failing at save time.

name: Workflow Participant Assignment (dynamic)
apex: A participant is named by role (e.g. Requisition Manager) but its actual value, one or more real users, is populated dynamically via a Code Editor expression or query rather than a fixed static list.
workflow: Developer writes a query or expression that returns the current holder(s) of a role so the workflow always routes to the right person without editing the definition.
relevance: Paddock's Moderation/Members approvals should resolve who can act the same way, e.g. a query for the post's category owner, instead of hardcoding a reviewer per request.

name: Copying a Workflow (cross-app)
apex: A wizard that copies an entire workflow, including all versions, parameters, activities, participants, variables and shared components, from another application into the current one.
workflow: Developer picks a source app and workflow, names the copy, and clicks Copy Workflow.
relevance: Paddock is a single application; there is no second workspace app to copy a workflow definition from.
skip_for_web: Multi-application reuse doesn't apply to a single-tenant Next.js site.

name: Workflow Activity Types (full catalog)
apex: The complete menu of activity types a developer can drop into a workflow: Custom Process Type Plug-in, Execute Code, Generate Text with AI, Human Task - Create, Invoke API, Invoke Workflow, Parallel Flow, Send Email, Send Push Notification, Switch, Wait, Workflow Start (exactly one, no incoming connections) and Workflow End (one or more, no outgoing connections).
workflow: Developer drags an activity type from the palette (or right-clicks Create Activity Below/After) and fills in the type-specific settings.
relevance: This catalog is the right checklist of primitive step types a Paddock approval-flow builder needs: a human decision step, a notify step, an external-call step, a branch, a delay, and a start/end pair with an explicit outcome.

name: Workflow End Activity (End State)
apex: An End activity must declare which of two End States it represents, Completed (normal success) or Terminated (abnormal/unexpected), so a workflow can have several distinct, explicitly-labeled endings rather than one generic exit.
workflow: Developer adds one End activity per distinct outcome (e.g. Approved-Complete vs Rejected-Terminated) instead of a single catch-all end point.
relevance: Paddock's approval flows should let a design distinguish multiple named end states (approved, rejected, withdrawn) rather than collapsing every outcome into one generic closed/done flag.

name: Workflow Switch Activity
apex: A branching activity with four condition styles: True False (a single boolean condition), Check Workflow Variable (branch on a variable's value with per-branch operators), Case (branch on a computed value across several data types), and If Elsif Else (AND/OR compound conditions), each branch created as a typed connection with its own evaluation Sequence.
attributes: Switch Type: True False/Check Workflow Variable/Case/If Elsif Else
workflow: Developer picks the switch style that matches the decision (simple boolean vs multi-way case vs compound logic) and adds one typed branch connection per outcome.
relevance: A content approval flow needs exactly this range of routing logic (simple yes/no review, route by category, compound rules); offering a few purpose-built condition builders beats one generic expression box.

name: Workflow Wait Activity
apex: An activity that pauses the workflow until either a configured Timeout elapses (Static ISO-duration, or computed via SQL Query/Expression/Function Body) or external code calls apex_workflow.continue_activity to resume it early.
workflow: Developer sets a wait activity's duration declaratively, or leaves it open-ended and resumes it programmatically from an API callback.
relevance: Directly useful for Paddock: auto-escalate a stalled moderation item after N days (timeout branch) while still letting an explicit action resume it early.

name: Human Task - Create Activity
apex: The activity that puts a human decision inside a workflow: it links to an existing Task Definition, can override the task's Subject/Priority/Initiator-Can-Complete, and auto-generates two workflow variables, TASK_OUTCOME (APPROVED/REJECTED) and APPROVER, that later Switch activities branch on.
workflow: Developer points a Human Task activity at a task definition, then adds a Switch right after it that checks TASK_OUTCOME to route to an approved or rejected path.
relevance: This is the exact primitive Paddock needs for author-request/post-review approvals: a step that waits for a person's decision and exposes a standard outcome + approver pair the rest of the flow can branch on.

name: Custom Process Type Plug-in as Activity
apex: Any process-type plug-in can become a first-class workflow step once its Supported For setting enables Workflow Activities; if it needs to run asynchronously, Wait for Completion pauses the workflow until the plug-in calls apex_workflow.continue_activity, invoking a configured Completion (or Termination) callback function.
workflow: Plug-in developer opts a process plug-in into workflow use and wires completion/termination callbacks; workflow developer then drops it in like any built-in activity.
relevance: A good extensibility model if Paddock's designer ever needs custom, code-defined steps (e.g. a bespoke fact-check integration) inside an otherwise declarative approval flow, sync or async.

name: Invoke Workflow Activity
apex: Calls another workflow (never itself or a caller, to prevent cycles) as a sub-process; Wait for Completion decides whether the parent blocks until it finishes; Retry Point (Resume vs Start Over) controls how a faulted invocation recovers; parameters pass through with an Ignore Output toggle for Out/In-Out values.
workflow: Developer composes a bigger process from smaller reusable workflows instead of duplicating steps, choosing whether the parent waits and how a failure is retried.
relevance: Sub-workflow composition is valuable if Paddock builds more than one approval flow (author request, post review, moderation) that share a common reusable step, e.g. a shared notify-and-wait sub-flow.

name: Activity Variables (third variable scope)
apex: A variable scoped to a single activity instance (Static ID, Label, Data Type, Value Type/Language, optional source Item, optional Boolean Format Mask), distinct from workflow-version Variables and workflow Parameters.
workflow: Developer adds an activity variable when a value is only meaningful within that one step, rather than promoting it to a workflow-wide variable.
relevance: A three-tier variable scoping model (app-wide input, flow-wide mutable state, single-step-local value) is a clean pattern Paddock's own approval-flow data model should copy instead of one flat bag of fields.

name: Creating the Workflow Console/Details/Dashboard Pages
apex: A Create Page Wizard component that generates all three pages at once, letting the developer pick the Report Context (My Workflows/Admin Workflows/Initiated by Me), whether to include the Dashboard, and the Details page's Form Page Mode (Normal, Modal Dialog, or Drawer).
workflow: Developer runs one wizard to scaffold the list, details and dashboard pages together instead of building each by hand.
relevance: Scaffolding an approval list + a details drawer/modal + a health dashboard as one generated unit (with a page-mode choice) is a good model for a Paddock Moderation/Members admin screen.

name: Editing Active vs In Development Versions
apex: An In Development version allows full edits (add/delete activities and connections, add/delete variables, delete the version); an Active version allows only a narrow safe subset: activity-local variables, switch branch conditions, and adding (not deleting) participants.
attributes: Active: activity variables/branch conditions/add participants only
workflow: Developer makes structural changes only in a draft version, but can still safely tweak routing logic or add reviewers to a version that's already live.
relevance: A precise, explicit list of which edits are safe to make live vs which require a new draft is exactly the safety rule Paddock needs before letting an admin edit an approval flow that has requests in flight.

name: Version Activation Guards and Import Suspension
apex: APEX blocks activating a workflow that invokes another workflow still In Development, and blocks deactivating a workflow that's invoked elsewhere unless a replacement draft exists; importing a new application version auto-suspends every running workflow instance rather than guessing whether the changed definition is still compatible, leaving resume/terminate to an administrator.
attributes: Activation blocked if invoked workflow lacks an Active version
Deactivation blocked if still relied upon
workflow: Administrator reviews each suspended instance after a redeploy and decides individually whether to resume or terminate it.
relevance: Two transferable safety rules for Paddock: block publishing a flow that depends on an unpublished piece, and never auto-resume in-flight approvals after a flow definition changes underneath them, always ask.

name: Workflow Page Process Actions (Start/Terminate/Suspend/Resume/Retry)
apex: A Workflow-type page process exposes five operations bindable to a button or action: Start (launches a new instance, binding each workflow Parameter to a page item/query/expression/static value), Terminate, Suspend, Resume (optionally at a specific Activity Static ID rather than where it paused), and Retry (for a Faulted instance).
workflow: Developer adds one page process per action needed and wires it to a button, binding start parameters from page items.
relevance: This is precisely the action set Paddock's approval UI needs as buttons on a request: start, cancel, pause, resume (optionally jumping to a specific step), and retry after an error.

name: Resuming Suspended Workflows at Any Activity
apex: APEX_WORKFLOW.RESUME accepts a target Activity Static ID, not just the activity where the workflow paused; resuming elsewhere terminates the current activity first. A worked example wires this to a Select List so a business admin can pick the resume point from a dropdown.
workflow: Administrator overrides the default resume point when a stuck approval needs to be manually nudged forward or backward to a specific step.
relevance: A manual override to jump a stuck approval to any step (not just retry from where it froze) is a valuable escape hatch for Paddock's Moderation console when an automated flow gets stuck.

name: Workflow Debug Messages (Instance ID column)
apex: A configurable column on the Debug Messages report that shows which workflow instance generated each debug line, so multi-instance debug logs can be filtered per run.
workflow: Developer sets a Debug Level on the workflow version, then adds the Workflow Instance column to Debug Messages to isolate one run's log lines.
relevance: Generic Oracle debug-log tooling; Paddock's own logging/observability stack (not APEX debug messages) is where equivalent per-request log correlation would live.
skip_for_web: APEX-specific debug console feature.

name: Workflow Utilization and History Reports
apex: Shared Components, Workflows page offers a Utilization tab (every page/component using a given workflow) and a History tab (recent modifications to workflow definitions), the same governance pair seen on Plug-ins and Automations.
workflow: Developer checks Utilization before changing a workflow, and History to see who last modified it.
relevance: Same Utilization/History component-governance pattern already logged for Plug-ins and Automations; no new concept, just another shared-component type repeating it.
skip_for_web: Duplicate of the generic component Utilization/History pattern.

name: Workflow Instance Retention
apex: A daily scheduled job keeps Active/Suspended/Faulted instances indefinitely, purges Completed instances after a configurable retention window (default 30 days, max 100), but purges Canceled and Terminated instances almost immediately, within one day, with no configurable grace period at all.
workflow: Instance administrator sets the retention period once in Instance Settings; canceled/terminated runs are not kept for audit beyond the next daily purge.
relevance: A useful asymmetry to copy: keep completed approval history for a real audit window, but don't bother giving canceled/terminated requests the same grace period since they carry little audit value.

name: Workflow Substitution Strings
apex: Built-in placeholders any page tied to a workflow instance can use to adapt its display: APEX$WORKFLOW_ID, APEX$WORKFLOW_STATE, APEX$WORKFLOW_ACTIVITY_ID, APEX$WORKFLOW_CREATED_ON, APEX$WORKFLOW_INITIATOR, APEX$WORKFLOW_DETAIL_PK (usable as a bind variable in activity/variable/participant queries).
workflow: Developer references these directly in page templates or conditions, e.g. showing a different region when APEX$WORKFLOW_STATE = 'FAULTED'.
relevance: Paddock's approval-flow pages should expose the same small set of always-available context values (instance id, state, initiator, created date, the record being approved) instead of each page re-fetching them manually.

name: Workflow Metadata and Runtime Views
apex: A family of dictionary views split into design-time metadata (APEX_APPL_WORKFLOWS, _VERSIONS, _ACTIVITIES, _TRANSITIONS, _BRANCHES, _VARIABLES, _PARAMS, _PARTICIPANT, etc.) and runtime instance data (APEX_WORKFLOWS, _ACTIVITIES, _VARIABLES, _PARTICIPANTS, _AUDIT, plus APEX_PURGEABLE_* variants for cleanup jobs).
workflow: Developer queries these views for custom reporting or to build purge jobs beyond the built-in retention policy.
relevance: Pure Oracle dictionary-view plumbing; the definition-vs-instance data split it reflects is already captured conceptually via the Workflow Definitions/Console notes.
skip_for_web: SQL view catalog, not a UI or design concept.

name: Workflow Designer Keyboard Shortcuts
apex: A full keyboard-accessible command set for the diagram editor: navigate between tree/diagram/messages/property-editor panes, move and connect activities, zoom, undo/redo, all without a mouse.
workflow: Keyboard-only developer opens the shortcut list and drives the whole diagram builder without a pointer.
relevance: Only matters if Paddock builds the full drag-and-drop diagram editor, which was already judged disproportionate for this site's scale; no shortcut list needed for a simpler config UI.
skip_for_web: Accessibility layer for a diagram editor Paddock isn't building.

name: Reimport Suspension: Auto-Resume vs Admin Decides
apex: Two doc pages describe app-reimport suspension slightly differently: the Versions page says an admin must manually resume or terminate every suspended instance because the definition may have changed; the FAQ says instances auto-resume once reimport finishes, framed as protection against transient unavailability. The likely reconciliation: redeploying an unchanged definition auto-resumes, but a structurally changed definition needs a human call.
attributes: Auto-resume (if unchanged) vs manual resume/terminate (if changed)
workflow: Developer treats a same-definition redeploy as safe to auto-resume, but flags any redeploy that changes an in-flight flow's shape for manual admin review.
relevance: Exactly the rule Paddock needs for editing a live approval flow: auto-resume in-flight requests after a no-op deploy, but force a human decision whenever the flow's steps actually changed underneath them.

name: Deadline Precedence: Workflow Overrides Task
apex: When both a workflow activity and its linked task definition specify a deadline, the workflow activity's deadline wins; a workflow-generated task is also always subject to expiration (even if the task definition's own expiration policy is NONE) and its due date can never be manually extended by an administrator, only auto-renewed per policy.
workflow: Developer relies on the workflow's own deadline setting when a task is embedded in a workflow, since the task's independent settings are subordinate.
relevance: A clear precedence rule for Paddock when the same setting (a due date) could be configured at two levels (the flow step vs the underlying task type): the containing flow always wins, and a human admin should not be able to silently override it.

name: Cancellation and Fault Cascades (landmine)
apex: Canceling a task hands the workflow no outcome value at all, so a following Switch checking TASK_OUTCOME faults rather than gracefully branching to a canceled path; an errored task also faults its parent workflow; terminating a workflow force-cancels every still-open task under it.
attributes: Canceled task: no outcome value (switch faults)
Terminated workflow: open tasks move to Canceled
workflow: Developer must explicitly model a canceled/withdrawn path (e.g. a timeout or error connection) since the engine won't default to one on its own.
relevance: A landmine worth avoiding in Paddock's own approval model: a withdrawn/canceled request needs its own explicit recognized state, not just a null decision, or downstream logic checking approve/reject will break; and closing a request should cascade-cancel any of its still-open sub-steps.

name: Manual Correction of a Mis-Clicked Approval
apex: If a workflow places a Wait activity right after an approval task, an administrator can suspend the workflow at that point, edit the auto-generated TASK_OUTCOME variable value directly from the Details page, and resume, effectively reversing an accidental approve/reject.
workflow: Administrator uses this only when the flow was deliberately designed with a pause point after the decision; otherwise there's no window to intervene.
relevance: A genuinely useful escape hatch for Paddock's Moderation console: build a brief pause after a decision step specifically so an admin can correct a fat-fingered approve/reject before it takes effect downstream.

name: Retry vs Resume (permissions) and Operational APIs
apex: Retry (for Faulted instances) can be run by either the Workflow Owner or Administrator with unlimited manual attempts and no auto-retry; Resume (for Suspended instances) is Administrator-only. Two more admin APIs: apex_workflow.refresh_participants re-evaluates dynamic participant queries against already-running instances, and apex_workflow.clear_test_data bulk-deletes instances created while a version was still In Development.
attributes: Retry: Owner or Administrator, Faulted only
workflow: Developer/administrator picks the right recovery action for the instance's actual state, and cleans up test instances or refreshes stale participant assignments via the two utility APIs.
relevance: Three small but concrete lessons for Paddock: give a broader set of people permission to retry a broken request than to resume a paused one, provide a way to re-resolve who's responsible on an already-open request, and give admins a one-click way to purge their own test approvals before going live.

name: Tasks (overview)
apex: A Human Task component for work only a person can do: Approval Tasks (owner Approves or Rejects) and Action Tasks (owner Completes), built from a Task Definition, a Unified Task List inbox page, a Task Details page, Human Task-Create/Manage page processes, and the APEX_HUMAN_TASK API; by default the initiator cannot complete their own task.
workflow: Developer configures a Task Definition, builds its list/details pages, then creates instances via a Human Task - Create page process; users act on them from their Unified Task List.
relevance: This is the most directly reusable APEX feature for Paddock's approvals: author requests and post reviews are Approval Tasks, moderation actions (e.g. remove a thread) are Action Tasks, each needing a definition, an inbox, and a details view.

name: Task States and Transitions
apex: A task moves Created (auto-splits to Unassigned if multiple potential owners, or Assigned if one) through intermediate states including Info Requested (owner asks the initiator for more detail, which resubmits back to Assigned) to a final state of Completed, Errored, Canceled, or Expired.
workflow: Users claim/delegate/release a task to move it between Unassigned and Assigned, request info when needed, and the engine auto-transitions to Expired if the due date passes.
relevance: The Info Requested state (send it back to the requester instead of just approve/reject) is a genuinely useful third outcome Paddock's author-request and post-review approvals are currently missing.

name: Task Expiration Policy: Expire vs Renew
apex: Each Task Definition sets what happens when a task's due date passes without completion: Expire (task ends, no replacement) or Renew (APEX automatically creates a fresh task instance, up to a configured maximum renewal count, after which it falls back to Expire); a Business Administrator can also manually Renew a task that ended in Errored.
workflow: Developer sets a renewal policy per task definition so stale approvals either die cleanly or automatically re-issue themselves a bounded number of times.
relevance: Directly solves a real Paddock need: an unreviewed author request or moderation item sitting too long should auto-re-notify (renew) a bounded number of times before finally expiring, instead of sitting silently forever.

name: Example: Approval and Action Tasks
apex: The sample app pairs a customized Task Details page (a Salary Change request showing a salary-history graph and percent change) against a standard, uncustomized one (Job Change), and demonstrates Initiator Can Complete turned on for a Bank Account change so the requester can approve their own low-risk request.
attributes: Customized vs standard Task Details page
Unified Task List contexts: My Tasks/My Requests/Task Administration
workflow: Developer decides per task type whether the generic details page is enough or a custom one adds relevant context, and whether self-approval is safe for that specific request type.
relevance: Confirms Task Details pages should be customizable per request type (e.g. show the actual post diff for a review, not just generic fields), and that self-approval should be a per-type toggle, not all-or-nothing.

name: Managing Tasks (TOC page)
apex: A navigation-only page linking to Task Definitions, Task Details, and Unified Task Lists; introduces no new concept beyond those three sub-topics.
relevance: Pure table-of-contents page; substance is captured under its child topics.
skip_for_web: Navigation page, no content of its own.

name: Managing Task Definitions (TOC page)
apex: A navigation-only page linking to About/Creating/Copying/Editing Task Definitions and their Utilization/History reports.
relevance: Pure table-of-contents page; substance is captured under its child topics.
skip_for_web: Navigation page, no content of its own.

name: Task Definition Participants (6 roles)
apex: A task definition names six distinct participant roles rather than a flat owner/admin split: Task Initiators (start it, can be asked for more info), Potential Owners (pool who may claim it), Actual Owner (whoever claimed it, can act on it), Business Administrators (can renew/reassign/cancel/reprioritize any task of this type), plus Excluded Owners and Excluded Admins to carve named exceptions out of a group rule; owners/admins can be a static user or an Authorization Scheme.
workflow: Developer assigns each role to a user, a dynamic query, or an authorization scheme, and uses Excluded Owner/Admin to exempt specific people from a broader group grant.
relevance: A much finer-grained role model than Paddock's current Members/Moderation likely has: a pool of eligible reviewers distinct from whoever actually claims an item, plus an explicit exception list to override a broad role grant for one person.

name: Vacation Rule (delegate-when-unavailable)
apex: A PL/SQL procedure returning alternate participants, settable at the task-definition level (overrides) or the whole-application level (default for every task definition); APEX runs it on task creation to add alternates to the participant pool, and on delegation to route to the first alternate returned.
workflow: Developer writes one procedure that checks an out-of-office flag or calendar and returns backup reviewers, wired once at the app level and overridden per task type only where needed.
relevance: A genuinely valuable pattern Paddock's Moderation lacks today: automatic backup-reviewer coverage when the usual approver is away, instead of a request silently stalling until they return.

name: Task Definition Actions (lifecycle event hooks)
apex: Each task definition can attach one or more Actions (Execute Code, Send Email, Send Push Notification, or a custom plug-in) to any of twelve lifecycle events (Create, Claim, Release, Delegate, Complete, Cancel, Update Comment/Priority/Parameter, Request Information, Submit Information, Before Expire, Expire), each with an execution Sequence, a Condition, and error handling (Stop Execution on Error, Log Messages When None/Success/Failure/All).
attributes: Action Type: Execute Code/Send Email/Send Push Notification/plug-in
workflow: Developer wires a notification or side-effect to a specific transition, e.g. emailing the initiator On Event = Complete, without touching the task's core logic.
relevance: An event-hook system on every state transition (not just approve/reject) is exactly what Paddock's approvals need: notify on claim, on request-for-info, on expire, each independently configurable instead of one hardcoded notification.

name: Task Type, Static ID, Priority, Initiator Can Complete
apex: Core identity fields set when creating a task definition: Type (Approval Task has an outcome; Action Task does not), a Static ID used to create instances programmatically via APEX_HUMAN_TASK.CREATE_TASK, a five-level Priority (1 Urgent to 5 Lowest, default 3 Medium), and, for approval tasks only, Initiator Can Complete (default Off).
attributes: Initiator Can Complete (Approval only, default Off)
workflow: Developer names the definition, sets whether it has a yes/no outcome, and decides per type whether the requester may approve their own request.
relevance: Confirms the Approval-vs-Action split and the self-approval toggle should be core fields on every Paddock approval type, not something bolted on later per feature.

name: Expiration Policy: None/Expire/Renew
apex: Three due-date behaviors, not two: None (default) leaves the task fully actionable past its due date; Expire locks it out from further action once due; Renew closes it and auto-creates a fresh instance, up to a Maximum Renewal Count of up to 99.
workflow: Developer picks None for soft deadlines that are just informational, Expire for hard cutoffs, or Renew for recurring reminders with a bounded retry count.
relevance: Paddock should offer this same three-way choice per approval type: some deadlines are advisory only, some are hard cutoffs, and some should auto-nag a bounded number of times before finally lapsing.

name: Task Definition Parameters
apex: Typed input fields for a task instance (Static ID, Label, Data Type, Required, Visible, Updatable, Comment); Visible controls whether it shows on the Task Details page and Updatable controls whether it can still be edited after the task has started.
workflow: Developer defines the data a task instance carries (e.g. the requested salary value) and independently controls whether it's shown and whether it's still editable mid-flight.
relevance: Splitting Visible from Updatable is a good fine-grained control Paddock's approval data model should copy: a field can be shown read-only for context without being editable after the request started.

name: Copying a Task Definition
apex: Duplicates a task definition's settings, deadline, participants, actions and parameters (copying along any shared components like email templates), but deliberately excludes the Task Details page and subscriptions, so the copy needs a page assigned before it's usable.
workflow: Developer copies a similar approval type as a starting point, then must still attach or build a details page for the new copy.
relevance: Cross-app copying doesn't apply to Paddock's single application; the selective what-copies-vs-what-doesn't nuance is a minor detail not worth building a feature around at this scale.
skip_for_web: Multi-application shared-component copy plumbing.

name: Task Definition Utilization and History Reports
apex: The same Utilization (where a definition is used) and History (recent modifications) tabs already seen on Plug-ins, Automations and Workflows, applied to Task Definitions.
workflow: Developer checks Utilization before changing a definition, History to see who last touched it.
relevance: Repeat of the generic component-governance pattern already logged multiple times this run; no new concept.
skip_for_web: Duplicate of the generic Utilization/History pattern.

name: Task Definition History Report
apex: Lists recent modifications made to Task Definitions in the current application, the same History-tab pattern as every other shared component type.
workflow: Developer opens History to see who last edited a given task definition.
relevance: Repeat of the generic component History-tab pattern already logged several times this run.
skip_for_web: Duplicate of the generic Utilization/History pattern.

name: Task Metrics via APEX_TASKS (worked example)
apex: A worked example wires an Execute Code action On Event = Complete that inserts into a custom metrics table by querying the APEX_TASKS runtime view with the bind variable :APEX$TASK_ID, capturing outcome, approver and elapsed days for later reporting.
workflow: Developer adds one Execute Code action that logs a metrics row every time a task of that type completes, then builds a normal report over the resulting table.
relevance: A clear pattern for a Paddock approvals dashboard: log a metrics row on every completed request (who, how long, what outcome) via a hook rather than deriving it later from scattered status history.

name: Task Details Page Actions (full button set)
apex: The generated Task Details page conditionally shows up to 16 buttons depending on task state and the viewer's role: Claim, Release, Delegate, Set Priority, Set Due Date, Request Information, Submit Information, Invite/Remove/Exclude Participant, Cancel, Renew, Comment, Update Parameter, plus Approve/Reject (approval tasks) or Save/Complete (action tasks).
workflow: APEX shows only the buttons valid for the task's current state and the logged-in user's role (owner vs business administrator), hiding the rest.
relevance: This is the definitive checklist of buttons a Paddock request/moderation details view needs, role- and state-gated, rather than a single generic Approve/Reject pair.

name: Editing the Task Details Page / Configuring Task History
apex: The Task Details page is just a generated Page Designer page a developer edits normally; task history logging is configured per-action via the same Log Messages When (None/Success/Failure/All) setting already defined on Task Definition Actions.
workflow: Developer edits the details page like any other page, and sets logging verbosity per action.
relevance: Both are restatements of concepts already logged (generated pages editable in Page Designer; Log Messages When under Task Definition Actions).
skip_for_web: Duplicate of already-captured concepts.

name: Unified Task List Contexts (My/Admin/Initiated by Me)
apex: Three built-in inbox views with distinct, non-obvious filter rules: My Tasks shows only Assigned-to-me or Unassigned-with-me-as-a-potential-owner tasks (approved/rejected/completed ones drop off, newest first); Admin Tasks shows everything the user administers including Errored/Completed/Canceled, with expired tasks hidden behind a Show expired tasks toggle; Initiated by Me shows every task the user started regardless of state.
attributes: Report Context: My Tasks/Admin Tasks/Initiated by Me
workflow: Developer generates the right inbox for each audience; a list can even live in a separate application from the task definitions if session sharing is configured.
relevance: The precise per-view filter rules (an active inbox hides finished items by default; an admin view keeps everything but hides expired behind a toggle; a requester view keeps full history) is exactly the design Paddock's My Requests / To Review / All Requests views should follow.

name: Creating/Editing Unified Task Lists (wizard)
apex: A Create Page Wizard component (Report Context, Name, Page Number, optional breadcrumb/navigation entries) that generates a Unified Task List page, afterward edited like any normal page in Page Designer.
workflow: Developer runs the wizard once per context needed, then customizes the generated page normally.
relevance: Mechanical page-generation wizard, the same Create Page Wizard pattern already covered for the Workflow Console; no new concept.
skip_for_web: Restates the generic Create Page Wizard flow.

name: Human Task - Create Page Process
apex: A page process that instantiates a task from a Task Definition on form submission: it can override Subject/Priority/Initiator Can Complete, set an Initiator Item so one user can raise a task on another's behalf, capture the new Task ID into a page item, and set a Details Primary Key Item that ties the task to one exact row of the definition's source table so approving it updates that specific record.
workflow: Developer attaches this process to a form's Submit button; on save, APEX creates a task instance linked to that exact record via the Details Primary Key.
relevance: This is the exact mechanism Paddock needs to turn a form submission (an author request, a post edit) into a trackable approval tied to one specific record, including letting staff file a request on a user's behalf.

name: Example: Human Task from a Form Submission
apex: A worked instantiation of the Human Task - Create process, conditioned to run only When Button Pressed = SUBMIT_FOR_APPROVAL rather than on every save, with the form's page item bound directly to the task's parameter.
workflow: Developer scopes task creation to one specific submit button among possibly several on the same form.
relevance: Restates the Human Task - Create Page Process concept already logged; the only addition (gating task creation on a specific button) is a minor, self-evident condition setting.
skip_for_web: Worked example of an already-captured concept.

name: APEX_HUMAN_TASK API Package
apex: A PL/SQL API for creating and managing task instances entirely from code, without a page process, covering both creation and lifecycle actions (claim, complete, cancel, etc.).
workflow: Developer calls the package from a trigger, a scheduled job, or another automation to raise or act on a task without a UI action.
relevance: Paddock will need an equivalent headless entry point to file or resolve an approval from code, e.g. auto-creating a moderation task when an automated content check flags a post.

name: Task Definition Process Plug-in
apex: A process-type plug-in with Type=Process and Supported for=Task Definition Actions becomes selectable as a Task Definition Action, letting a developer package repeated logic (e.g. updating an external system on approval) into one reusable declarative action instead of pasting the same PL/SQL into every task definition that needs it.
workflow: Plug-in developer builds the integration once; task definition authors just pick it from the Action Type list instead of writing custom code each time.
relevance: Reinforces the plug-ins lesson directly for approvals: common notification/integration hooks (e.g. posting to the site's own webhook or activity log) should be built once as a reusable action, not copy-pasted per approval type.

name: Task Retention Policy
apex: A daily job keeps Active/Unassigned/Assigned tasks indefinitely, purges Completed tasks after a configurable retention period (default 7 days, max 30), and purges Terminated/Canceled/Errored tasks almost immediately (within the next daily run, well under 24 hours) with no configurable grace period.
workflow: Instance administrator sets the completed-task retention window; nothing can be done to extend retention for terminated/canceled/errored tasks.
relevance: Same asymmetric retention lesson as Workflow Retention, applied to individual approvals: keep resolved-approval history for a real window, but don't bother extending that grace period to abandoned or failed ones.

name: Archive of Purged Task Files (pre-delete export)
apex: Before the daily purge job deletes eligible tasks, APEX writes a JSON archive of them to a Purged Task Files report in Workspace Administration (itself cleaned up after 30 days); developers can also proactively copy soon-to-be-purged rows into their own table by querying APEX_PURGEABLE_TASKS ahead of the purge.
workflow: Developer either relies on the 30-day JSON archive as a safety net, or merges purgeable rows into a permanent history table before they're deleted.
relevance: A better retention pattern than a hard delete: auto-export to a JSON/cold-storage archive right before purging, giving Paddock a recovery window instead of permanently losing old approval records the instant retention expires.

name: Task Substitution Strings and Bind Variables
apex: A dozen-plus context placeholders available on any task-related page or query, including the usual ID/STATE/OWNER/INITIATOR/SUBJECT/DUE_ON, plus two less obvious ones: APEX$TASK_PREVIOUS_ID chains a renewed task back to the expired task it replaced, and APEX$TASK_TEXT carries the actual comment/request-info/submit-info message text so a follow-up Execute Code or Send Email action can quote it.
workflow: Developer references these in the task details page, action code, or email templates instead of re-querying the task instance manually.
relevance: The renewal-chain link and the reusable comment-text placeholder are worth copying directly: Paddock's renewed/escalated approvals should keep a traceable link to what they replaced, and a rejection comment should be quotable in the notification it triggers.

name: Task Runtime Views (definition vs actual roster)
apex: APEX_TASKS/_COMMENTS/_HISTORY/_PARAMETERS/_PARTICIPANTS runtime views mirror the workflow ones, with one notable nuance: APEX_TASK_PARTICIPANTS can differ from the task definition's configured participants, because a Business Administrator can invite or remove participants on a single running instance.
workflow: Developer queries these for custom reporting; an admin's per-instance participant edits show up here even though they never touch the underlying definition.
relevance: A good data-modeling nugget: separate a task/approval type's default participant list (the template) from one specific request's actual, potentially admin-edited roster (the instance), rather than only ever reading the template.

name: Troubleshooting: Identity Case-Sensitivity and Job Session Context
apex: Two operational landmines: (1) task authorization compares participant identities as exact strings, so a participant configured in the wrong case than the logged-in username produces a false Not Authorized error even though the user is genuinely the right person; (2) calling apex_human_task APIs from a DBMS Scheduler job fails with Task Not Found because a scheduled job has no APEX session, and must first call apex_session.create_session with the acting username before approving/rejecting.
workflow: Developer normalizes identity case before comparing, and always establishes an explicit session/acting-user context before calling approval APIs from a background job.
relevance: Two landmines worth avoiding in Paddock: never compare Clerk user IDs/roles with case-sensitive string equality, and any cron/background code that acts on an approval on someone's behalf must explicitly set who it's acting as rather than assuming an ambient session.

name: Troubleshooting: Expiration Sweep Latency
apex: A task's due date passing doesn't immediately flip it to Expired; APEX only checks for overdue tasks via an hourly background job, so a manual API, APEX_HUMAN_TASK.HANDLE_TASK_DEADLINES, exists specifically to force that check on demand for testing.
workflow: Developer calls the manual API while testing an expiration policy instead of waiting up to an hour for the real sweep to run.
relevance: A due-date-based state change should be documented as eventually consistent (checked on a sweep interval, not instantaneous), and Paddock should give itself the same kind of on-demand force-check hook for testing auto-expiry logic.

name: Administrator Security Best Practices (chapter overview)
apex: A table-of-contents page introducing the Security chapter's administrator-facing topics: admin roles, ORDS/web-server security, instance security, instance settings, workspace purge settings, workspace management, BI Publisher SSL integration, the runtime-environment's reduced admin surface, and enabling database network services.
workflow: An instance administrator works through these sub-topics when hardening a self-hosted APEX instance.
relevance: Pure navigation page over Oracle Cloud/self-hosted-instance administration; Paddock has no APEX-style multi-workspace hosting layer to secure the same way.
skip_for_web: Instance/workspace hosting administration, out of scope for a single-tenant Next.js site.

name: Administrator Roles (Workspace vs Instance)
apex: Two admin tiers: Workspace administrators manage user accounts, activity and logs within one shared workspace; Instance administrators are superusers managing an entire hosted APEX instance (all workspaces) via Administration Services, a role that doesn't even exist on Oracle's own Database Cloud Service.
workflow: A hosting provider or DBA operates at the instance level; day-to-day app/user administration happens at the workspace level.
relevance: This two-tier model exists because one APEX instance hosts many independent workspaces; Paddock is a single site with one Clerk-role hierarchy, so there is no equivalent instance-vs-workspace split to copy.
skip_for_web: Multi-tenant hosting administration model, not applicable to a single site.

name: Web Server Security: Callable-Procedure Allow List
apex: Oracle recommends configuring the ORDS/PL-SQL gateway's security.requestValidationFunction to ords_util.authorize_plsql_gateway, which activates a built-in allow-list of callable procedures and blocks every other procedure from being invoked by an incoming web request.
workflow: Administrator sets this one configuration parameter when deploying the web gateway so unlisted server procedures can never be reached from the network.
relevance: The specific ORDS/PL-SQL gateway mechanics don't apply, but the underlying principle transfers directly: Paddock's API routes should be an explicit, minimal allow-listed surface rather than anything reachable-by-default.
skip_for_web: ORDS-specific configuration parameter; the transferable idea is only the allow-list principle.
